h1: Drywall Repair & Installation in Leander, TX
intro: Most drywall calls we get are small: a doorknob through the wall, a crack over a doorway, a ceiling stain after a roof leak. Those repairs are easy to do and easy to do badly — a patch that doesn't match the surrounding texture is more obvious than the hole was. We match texture before we finish, so the repair disappears into the wall.

process: Look at it
Add photos to your estimate request and we can usually tell you what it needs before we drive out. Bigger jobs get a walk-through.
Written estimate
You get the price in writing before anything starts. No hourly surprises.
Repair and texture
We cut back to solid material, patch, and match the existing texture — not a generic finish.
Clean up
Drywall dust travels. We contain the work area and leave the room clean.
faq: How much does drywall repair cost in Leander TX?

It depends on the size and whether texture matching is involved. A small hole patch is a very different job from a water-damaged ceiling section. We give a written estimate before starting, and we'll tell you honestly if a repair is small enough to handle yourself.
Can you match my existing wall texture?

Yes. Texture matching is the part most repairs get wrong. We identify the existing texture — orange peel, knockdown, skip trowel, or smooth — and match it before finishing, so the patch isn't visible once painted.
Do you repair water-damaged ceilings?

Yes. We cut out the damaged section back to solid material, replace it, texture to match, and paint. If the leak is still active, that needs to be fixed first — we'll tell you if that's the case rather than covering it up.
How fast can you get out here?
For small repairs in the Leander, Cedar Park, and Georgetown area we can usually schedule within the same week. Request an estimate with a few photos and we'll tell you what we can do.
Do you paint after the repair?
Yes. We can prime and paint the repaired area, or repaint the full wall if matching an aged paint color would leave a visible patch.

faq: How much does it cost to paint a house interior in Leander TX?

It varies with square footage, ceiling height, how much prep and repair the walls need, and whether trim and ceilings are included. We give a written estimate itemized by area so you can see exactly what's included rather than a single lump number.
How long does an interior repaint take?
A single room is often a day. A full interior repaint on an average Leander home typically runs several days depending on prep, trim, and ceilings. We give you a schedule with the estimate.
Do you paint kitchen cabinets?
Yes. Cabinets need degreasing, sanding, and a bonding primer to hold up to daily use — it's a different process from wall painting, and shortcuts on cabinets show fast.
What time of year is best for exterior painting in Central Texas?
Spring and fall are ideal. Mid-summer heat can cause paint to dry too fast and affect adhesion, so exterior work in July and August is scheduled for earlier in the day.

Yes. We handle unit turns for property managers across the Austin metro, including paint, drywall repair, and flooring on a turn schedule.

intro: Central Texas is hard on concrete and siding — limestone dust, hard water, pollen, and mildew on anything shaded. Pressure washing is the cheapest thing you can do to make a property look maintained, and on a home going up for sale it's usually the highest-return hour of work on the whole punch list.

faq: How much does pressure washing cost in Leander TX?

It's priced by area and surface type. A driveway is straightforward; a two-story house with stained siding takes longer and requires soft washing. We give a written estimate rather than a phone guess.
Will pressure washing damage my siding?
It can, if the wrong pressure is used. Siding, stucco, and painted surfaces are soft washed at lower pressure with cleaning solution rather than blasted. Concrete takes higher pressure.
How often should a driveway be pressure washed?
In Central Texas, most homeowners are happy with once a year. Shaded areas that grow mildew, and commercial properties with foot traffic, benefit from twice.
Do you do commercial and recurring contracts?
Yes. We handle parking lots, dumpster pads, sidewalks, and building exteriors on scheduled contracts for commercial and multi-family properties, and for government facilities under NIGP 968-94.
Should I pressure wash before selling my house?
Almost always. It's inexpensive relative to its effect on listing photos and first impressions, and it's one of the few pre-listing items that pays for itself visibly.

intro: Most flooring complaints are not about the flooring. They are about what was underneath it and nobody looked: a subfloor that was never levelled, a transition cut short, a bathroom where the tile was laid over a soft spot. We check the floor before we quote the floor, and we tell you what we find even when it makes the job bigger than you hoped.

process: Measure and look underneath
We measure the rooms and check what is under the existing floor. A soft subfloor or an uneven slab changes the job, and it is cheaper to know now.
Written estimate
Material and labour in writing, including the tear-out, the transitions and the trim — the parts that usually turn up as an extra later.
Prep, then install
Levelling and subfloor repair first. Flooring laid over a bad substrate fails, and it fails as your problem rather than the floor's.
Trim and finish
Transitions, base and thresholds done properly, and the room cleaned and put back.
faq: How much does flooring installation cost in Leander TX?

It depends on the material, the square footage, and what is under the old floor. LVP over a flat, sound subfloor is at the cheaper end; tile in a wet area, or anything needing the slab levelled, costs more. You get the number in writing before anything starts.
Can you install flooring over my existing floor?

Sometimes, and often it is a bad idea. Going over tile or an old floating floor raises the height at every door and transition and hides whatever is failing underneath. We will tell you honestly whether it is reasonable in your case.
Do you move the furniture?
Yes, for normal household furniture. Pianos, safes, and anything that needs disassembly we talk about beforehand so it is in the estimate rather than a surprise on the day.
What about the baseboards?
We can pull and reinstall existing base, or install new. Old base often does not survive removal intact, so we say up front which way we expect it to go.
How long does a floor take?
A single room is usually a day. A whole house is several, and tile takes longer than plank because of the set and cure time. The estimate gives you the schedule, not just the price.

h1: Deck & Patio Builder in Leander, TX
intro: Central Texas is hard on an outdoor build. Sun splits boards on the south side, the clay moves under the footings, and a deck put together with the wrong fasteners starts working loose in a couple of summers. The difference between a deck that lasts and one that sags is almost entirely in the parts you stop being able to see once it is finished.

process: Walk the space
We look at the ground, the drainage and the attachment point at the house. What a deck sits on decides how long it lasts.
Written scope and estimate
Materials, footings, framing and finish, written down. You will know what you are getting rather than what the photo looked like.
HOA and permits first
Most Leander and Cedar Park HOAs want a submittal for anything structural outdoors, and some builds need a permit. We tell you which applies before work starts, not after a letter arrives.
Build and finish
Framing, decking, rail and stairs, then the site cleaned. Offcuts and old material hauled away.
faq: How much does a deck cost to build in Leander TX?

Size, height off the ground, and material drive most of it — a ground-level pressure-treated deck and an elevated composite deck with railing are different jobs at different prices. We quote in writing after seeing the space.
Composite or wood?

Composite costs more up front and almost nothing to maintain, which suits a west-facing deck that bakes all afternoon. Wood is cheaper and looks better to a lot of people, and it needs sealing. Neither is the right answer for everyone.
Do I need HOA approval for a deck?

In most Leander and Cedar Park neighbourhoods, yes, for anything structural. It is usually straightforward, and far easier before the build than after. We will tell you what your HOA typically asks for.
Can you repair a deck instead of replacing it?

Often, and it is worth asking. If the frame and footings are sound, resurfacing is a fraction of a rebuild. If the structure is going, replacing boards on top of it is money spent twice — we will say which one you have.
How long does a deck take?
A straightforward build is usually several days once materials are on site. Covers, stairs and anything needing footings to cure take longer. The schedule is in the estimate.
